occlusion_stop_law.one_liner: Walking BUILD depth d=0..3 front-to-back, the view is VISIBLE for depths [0 .. stop], where `stop` is the FIRST depth whose forward edge OCCLUDES (inclusive). If no depth occludes, all four are visible. occludes(d) := front==2 OR (front==3 AND cornerL_solid AND cornerR_solid).
occlusion_stop_law.ceiling_floor_emit: For each visible depth d the engine emits the ceiling twin (placement 122+d) and the floor twin (150+d). These are gated INSIDE wall_emit_quad by the per-depth visibility byte [bx+0x5042] (bx=depth*3+1) at 0x407d (cmp byte [bx+0x5042],0; jne skip-ceiling).
occlusion_stop_law.front_code_meaning: 0=open passage, 2=solid stone wall, 3=door/special edge (1 also a door-class edge). cornerL/cornerR = the perpendicular wall edges of the viewed cell (classify_corner_L 0x3c11 / classify_corner_R 0x3dce; see maze-geometry.ts cornerL/cornerR for the per-facing dispatch).
occlusion_stop_law.why_door_caps_or_not: A door (code 3) read HEAD-ON in a corridor that is solid on BOTH lateral corners is a CLOSED DOORWAY — a wall with a door-shaped recess that the view cannot see past (it occludes). The SAME door code where one corner is OPEN is a passage opening / T-junction mouth, which the view sees through (it does NOT occlude). This is the geometric manifestation of occ_seed_front's two-pronged condition (front==2 || the door-frame corner gate [0x5067]).

findings.claim: The per-depth VISIBILITY of the ceiling/floor twins is a front-to-back occlusion: depths [0 .. stop] are visible, stop = first depth whose forward edge OCCLUDES (front==2 solid OR front==3 with BOTH corners solid = a closed doorway). PROVEN byte-exact vs all 4 parity-EVEN captures' ceiling-depth SETs: v1 [0,1,2] (door-cap at d2, both corners solid), v2 [0,1,2,3] (door at d1 has cornerR open -> NOT a cap), v5 [0,1] (solid wall cap at d1), v6 [0] (closed-door cap at d0). The visible depths derived from the maze block (computeVisibleDepths) EQUAL the captured ceiling depths for every view.

evidence.details: 0x407d cmp byte [bx+0x5042],0; jne skip-ceiling (bx=depth*3+1) gates the per-depth ceiling/floor emit inside wall_emit_quad 0x406c. occ_seed_front 0x4892(front,depth): 0x4895 cmp [bp+6],2 je SEED; 0x489b cmp [bp+6],5 jge SEED; else 0x48ac cmp byte [depth*3+0x5067],1 jne RET — i.e. SEED (clear deeper gates + lower the depth bound [0x521e] to depth+3) when front==2 OR (front<5 AND the door-frame corner gate [0x5067] is set). The corner gate [0x5067] is the byte-level manifestation of 'both corners solid' (the classifier sets it for a door framed by solid walls). Captured ceiling depths (placementIndices containing 122+d): v1={0,1,2}, v2={0,1,2,3}, v5={0,1}, v6={0}. computeVisibleDepths(BLOCK, party) returns EXACTLY these (test: index-arithmetic.test.ts 'the visible depths match the captured ceiling depths exactly').

findings.claim: The v1-vs-v2 difference (door at depth 2 CAPS the view in v1; door at depth 1 does NOT cap in v2) is NOT distance-keyed and NOT a clean function of the forward-edge profile alone — it is whether the door is FRAMED by solid corners on both sides. v1's door cell (gy123) has cornerL=2 AND cornerR=2 (a closed doorway in a corridor -> occludes). v2's door cell (gy120) has cornerL=2 but cornerR=0 (a doorway at a T-junction / passage opening -> see-through, does NOT occlude). So the occlusion predicate must read the corner edges, not just the front code. This is the precise discriminator the task flagged as 'depth-walked occlusion, not a clean function of the edge profile.'

evidence.details: Per-depth cell-data via maze-geometry.ts forwardEdge/cornerL/cornerR on extracted/maze/level-0.json. v1: d2 cell(127,123) front=3 cL=2 cR=2 -> closed doorway -> stop at d2 (visible [0,1,2]). v2: d1 cell(127,120) front=3 cL=2 cR=0 -> open-cornered door -> NOT a stop (visible [0,1,2,3]). findings.claim: The BUILD depth loop body (wmaze 0x4d90..0x5059) calls the emit fns in a fixed order, EACH gated by a per-depth gate BYTE indexed by the depth counter [0x5040]: (1) front wall_emit_quad 0x406c gated by [depth+0x508a]==1; then occ_seed_front 0x4892. (2) corner-L wall_emit_corner 0x45b4 gated by [depth+0x508a]==1; then occ_seed_2 0x48f5. (3) corner-R 0x45b4 gated by [depth+0x508a]==1; then occ_seed_3 0x4926. (4) left-side emit 0x47a3 gated by [depth+0x5082]==1. (5) left-side wall_emit_quad 0x406c gated by [depth+0x5072]==1; then occ_seed_4 0x4957. (6) right-side path gated by [depth+0x5092]/[0x509a]; then occ_seed_5 0x4984. So the FRONT gate [0x508a] drives the front wall + BOTH corners (the near full-height wall + door-recess flanks); the side gates [0x5072]/[0x5082]/[0x5092] drive the per-depth side-wall families. These gate bytes are SEEDED by the classifier post-pass (0x3931 clears [0x5072/0x507a/0x5082], 0x3946 clears [0x508a], 0x3951 clears [0x5092/0x509a/0x50a2]) based on the per-slot code dispatch — this is the medium-confidence residue for the side/corner/door family emission.
